children: German exports in July retreated for the first time since January, slowing a nascent recovery in net trade that helped drive the country's economic growth in the first half of the year.
Exports declined 0.8% on month in July to 138.2 billion euros, or $160.62 billion, Germany's statistics agency said Tuesday.

However, a steeper 5.7% decline in imports widened the country's trade surplus to 21.3 billion euros, from 15.4 billion euros in June, supporting gross domestic product growth at the start of the third quarter.

Goods exports to fellow European Union nations, alongside the U.K. and China, all fell back, but exports to the U.S. jumped almost 20% on month. President Trump announced a fresh 10% tariff on EU goods imports in July, replacing temporary levies imposed in February, potentially contributing to front-running among importers.

Net exports had contributed to Germany's growing economy in the first two quarters of the year as the Iran conflict caused severe supply-chain disruptions for Asian competitors, benefiting manufacturers in Germany. Companies also stockpiled inventory in anticipation of higher costs due to the war.

The data suggest a continuing rebound in net exports this year--having dragged in 2024 and 2025-- even if the numbers are volatile and more evidence will be needed of a sustained fall in imports, Pantheon Macroeconomics economist Claus Vistesen said in a note to clients.
"We also suspect that the leap in exports to the U.S. will reverse in the coming months," Vistesen added.

Still, German factory orders climbed for a third-straight month in July, data published last week showed, indicating continued demand for the country's goods despite the high energy costs and geopolitical headwinds prompted by the conflict.

Export expectations in August rose to their highest level since February 2022, driven by electrical and digital manufacturers as artificial-intelligence investment surges, the Ifo Institute said last month.
"The upward trend has paused. After the gains of the previous months, this is quite normal," said Alexander Krueger, chief economist at Bethmann HAL.
"The greatly improved sentiment among exporters suggests continued strong foreign demand," he said. "Exports are still expected to contribute to growth."

title: German Exports Decline for First Time in Six Months — Update
